open_obligations: Note the pilot-study caveat stated by Kirchner et al.
Check whether sneaky-prover flaws resemble natural errors more than human-inserted bugs do.
Note the domain change from code to grade-school math.
in.other_title: Sneaky prover flaws get harder for time-limited humans to spot over rounds (pilot study)
in.rationale: McAleese et al. note human-inserted bugs differ from natural LLM errors and suggest training models to insert subtle in-distribution problems. Kirchner et al. report sneaky-prover solutions become harder for time-limited humans to label correctly over rounds and suggest the sneaky prover could serve as a tampering model for training critique models; this comes from a pilot study with design flaws, on math rather than code.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a trained model can generate subtle flaws for training critics instead of humans inserting bugs, for sneaky provers on grade-school math

text: The authors state that a key limitation is that the distribution of inserted bugs is quite different from that of natural LLM errors. They suggest training models to insert subtle in-distribution problems instead of paying humans to insert bugs, and leave this to future work.
title: Human-inserted bugs differ from the distribution of natural LLM errors
